newsitem.title: USA: Humana's profits for quarter, year fall due to charges.
newsitem.headline: Humana's profits for quarter, year fall due to charges.

text.p: Humana Inc., one of the nation's largest managed health care companies, said Tuesday that profits fell sharply in the fourth quarter and for all of 1996, mainly due to charges for restructuring.

The company said net income for quarter ended Dec. 31 fell 55 percent to $22 million, or 13 cents a share, from $49 million, or 30 cents a share, after it took a $10 million after-tax charge in the latest quarter related to the planned elimination of up to 900 jobs this year.
For the full year Humana said net income plunged 94 percent to $12 million, 7 cents a share, from $190 million, or $1.17 a share. The 1996 results included charges of $130 million.
Revenues rose to $1.81 billion in the quarter from $1.49 billion and to a record $6.79 billion from $4.70 billion.
Total operating expenses grew 26 percent to $1.78 billion from $1.41 billion in the quarter and 54 percent to $6.76 billion from $4.40 billion for the year, Humana said.

Premium revenues for the quarter grew 22 percent to $1.8 billion from $1.5 billion -- primarily due to revenues earned under Humana's contract with the Pentagon's Civilian Health and Medical Programme.
It said membership at the end of the year totalled a record 4.9 million, up from 3.8 million a year earlier.
Medicare risk membership grew by 54,100 members, or 17 percent -- more than double the previous year's growth of 23,000 members, or 8 percent.

However, commercial membership fell by 31,600 members during the quarter and by 69,100 for the entire year, mainly as a result of higher prices and the company's planned exit from unprofitable markets.
"Our plans to withdraw from certain markets and price business commensurate with the underlying risk are proceeding on schedule," President Gregory Wolf said in a statement.

"Commercial membership will decrease an additional 115,000 members during the remainder of the first quarter, primarily as a result of the sale of our Washington, D.C., and Alabama operations. After these two sales are completed, commercial membership should begin to grow modestly," he added.
The company offers various health care plans to employer groups, government entities and individuals.
Humana's stock rose 62.5 cents to $19 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
